html:
Mutara III Rudahigwa was king of Rwanda from 1931, when the Belgians deposed his father Yuhi Musinga, until his sudden death in 1959.

His father had resisted the missions. Rudahigwa was baptised a Catholic in 1943, chiefs and people followed in a wave of conversions, and in 1946 he dedicated the country to Christ the King. The Catholic Church became the strongest institution in Rwanda.

He abolished cattle clientship in 1954 and began to press for independence, which cooled Belgian support for the Tutsi elite. He died in July 1959 in Bujumbura after a medical injection, and many Tutsi suspected murder. His death opened the crisis that led to the Rwandan Revolution and the end of the monarchy.
